newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics begins shipping x2 modems.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics begins shipping x2 modems.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp said Monday it had begun shipping its proprietary x2 modem technology, which allows Internet connections at 56 kilobits per second, or roughly twice as fast over telephone lines as current modems.

The company said it had begun shipments to North American retailers. It said it plans to demonstrate a European version of x2 at the CeBIT trade show in Germany in March, with distribution in European and Pacific Rim markets to follow.
U.S. Robotics's pioneering x2 modem technology faces a battle for acceptance versus a similar technology backed by an alliance of rivals led by Rockwell International Corp.
Allies of Rockwell include Lucent Technologies Inc and Motorola Inc. The alliance has announced plans to introduce 56 kilobit modems in early March.

While in the long run the modem makers are expected to come to agreement on a common standard for 56-kilobit technology, U.S. Robotics modems are currently incompatible with modems made by those in the Rockwell alliance.

U.S. Robotics said the x2 technology gives it a significant head start over its rivals because older modems it has been shipping since August 1996 can be converted to run the higher speed x2 technology by a simple software upgrade.

Announcing the shipment of x2, U.S. Robotics Chairman and Chief Executive Casey Cowell criticized his company's rivals for "causing consumer confusion by raising unwarranted fears of obsolescence or incompatibility."
"That argument is a smokescreen," Cowell said. "The ability to connect is the real issue and with U.S. Robotics, consumers can connect and stay connected regardless of the standard."

U.S. Robotics said the software upgrade feature of x2 technology gives the company a distinct advantage over rivals' hardware-based 56-kilobit modem technology, which becomes fixed at the time the modem device is built.
U.S. Robotics is the world's largest supplier of consumer modems.
Rockwell is a leading supplier of chipsets used to create built-in computer modems.
